game_structure: Maldita Castilla uses GameMaker GEN8 with data.win (47.1 MB)
boss_mechanics: Alarm-driven phase systems (Luzfarel 7-phase, Heart 4-phase, Demon Court 3-phase)
convergence: Use GameMaker VM bytecode as native target
Parallax background with y=320 offset for proper ground alignment
Player physics with origin at bottom, body offset (-7, -34) for feet alignment
Single continuous ground collision body spanning entire level (prevent player stuck on seams)
Touch controls with large buttons (100px), visual feedback
Enemy path system with GML-style movement patterns
Alarm-driven boss phase transitions (similar to Luzfarel, Heart, Demon Court phases)
Collisions based on bullet groups (Collision_48 for regular, Collision_0 for knives, etc.)
Animation system (idle=0, walk=1-4, jump=5-7, attack=8-10, crouch=11, hurt=12-14, die=15)
differences: VEGA 3D engine vs custom Phaser 2D renderer
48MB GameMaker assets vs compressed web assets
GameMaker VM bytecode vs hand-written GML bytecode
Touch arcade machine vs mobile touch controls
Collision-based object system vs Phaser physics engine
GameMaker data.win vs file-based asset system
VEGA GameMaker API vs custom backend API
conclusion: Both projects share identical gameplay mechanics with different technical implementations
